attributes.refutation_evidence: The superseded record's own sample rows pair instructions that BOTH EXIST IN BOTH STREAMS, which is the signature of a reorder, not a codegen-form gap: its row `0x0070 OPCODE-DIFFERS: T lha r7,10(r31) / O lhz r0,18(r31)` is contradicted by regnorm's own UNPAIRED lists, where `lha r7,10(r31)` appears as UNPAIRED-O @0x0094 and `lhz r0,18(r31)` as UNPAIRED-T @0x00a0. Same for its rows at 0x0090, 0x00a8, 0x0164 and 0x0174. Its READING ('different opcode - a real codegen-form gap, not a colouring') is therefore WRONG for all 4 OPCODE-DIFFERS rows. POSITIVE AUDIT, all three checks clean: (1) memory-access (opcode,displacement) multiset IDENTICAL over all 141 parsed instructions - no wrong field read anywhere; (2) immediate/operand-constant multiset IDENTICAL - no wrong constant; (3) relocation set IDENTICAL for every call - GXBegin, GXLoadPosMtxImm, GXSetChanMatColor, PSMTXIdentity, SetCullMode, SetMultiPassTextureParams, SetPerspectiveMode, SetVertexFormat, SetViewportHeight, plus _savefpr_27/_restfpr_27 and gWinGlobals. The ONLY reloc delta is that target names lbl_80348A88 (.double 4503599627370496 = 2^52) and lbl_80348A98 (.double 4503601774854144 = 2^52+2^31) where our TU emits equivalent anonymous pool entries; our stream carries the identical `lis 17200` / `xoris 32768` int-to-double idiom with matching immediates, so this is cosmetic pool naming, not a value difference.
